title: Isaiah 46:1–13
context: After 45:14–25—the wealth of Egypt and the merchandise of Cush, and the Sabeans, men of stature, shall come over; Truly, you are a God who hides himself, O God of Israel, the Savior; Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth; every knee shall bow, every tongue swear; in the LORD all the offspring of Israel shall be justified and shall glory—the word turns: Bel bows down; Nebo stoops; their idols are on beasts and livestock, borne as burdens on weary beasts. Listen, O house of Jacob, borne from before birth; even to old age I will carry you; declaring the end from the beginning; calling a bird of prey from the east.

voices.heading: Voices from both camps
voices.intro: Historic words on Bel bowing and Nebo stooping, idols borne as burdens on weary beasts, the house of Jacob carried from the womb even to old age, none like him, declaring the end from the beginning, a bird of prey from the east, and salvation put in Zion for Israel his glory—so each camp speaks in its own voice beside Isaiah 46:1–13.
voices.note: Quotations lightly abridged for length; wording follows standard English translations of the sources named.

arminian.quote: Bel—The chief idol of the Babylonians, called by profane historians Jupiter Belus. Boweth—As the Babylonians used to bow down to him to worship, so now he bows down to the victorious Persians. Nebo—Another of the famous idols, which used to deliver oracles. Their idols—Were taken and broken, and the materials of them, gold, silver, and brass, were carried upon beasts into Persia. Your carriages—O ye Persians, to whom he turns his speech. They—The Babylonians. Together—The Babylonians and their idols together, neither could help the other. Deliver—The Babylonians could not deliver their idols. Carried—Whom I have nourished, ever since you were a people, and came out of Egypt; and that as tenderly, as parents bring up their own children. Remove—He can stir neither hand nor foot to help his people. Bring it—Think of this again and again, ye who have been guilty of this foolish sin. Declaring—Foretelling from the beginning of the world, future events which should happen in succeeding ages, even to the end of the world. A bird—Cyrus, called a bird for his swiftness, and ravenous for his fierceness, and victoriousness over his enemies. I bring—Tho’ you are unrighteous, I will shew myself a righteous and faithful God, making good my promise of delivering you out of Babylon after seventy years. It—My work of saving you from the Babylonish captivity. Will place—I will bring my people to Zion, and save them from all their enemies. My glory—In whom I will once again glory as my people.
arminian.source: Explanatory Notes upon the Old Testament (on Isa 46:1–13)

reformed.quote: Bel and Nebo: idols worshipped by the Babylonians, their chief patrons; Nebo perhaps inferior to Bel as Mercury to Jupiter. Fulfilled when Persians and Medes took Babylon by storm; idols taken as booty. Isaiah also looked farther to the coming of Christ, when all false worship falls (2 Cor 6:14). Idols cannot withdraw from the burden; no strength or motion; contrast with the true God who needs nothing. Soul gone into captivity: ironic, they have neither soul nor understanding. Ark taken by Philistines is not the same: ark was a symbol leading up to God in heaven, not adored as God. Hear me: vast difference—Babylon’s gods must be drawn on carts; the God of Israel carries his people like a mother who carries the child in her womb and then in her bosom. From the womb: not only nurse from birth but spiritually begot them (James 1:18) into new life. Remnant of the house of Israel: greater part alienated by revolt; hope of deliverance belonged only to a very small number. Even to old age: guardian till the end; he completes what he has begun (Ps 138:8; 22:10; 71:9). I am the same: always like himself, not only in essence but toward us. I have made and will carry: he created them to be his children, and will continue a father’s and mother’s care. To whom will ye liken me: they distrusted his power when they saw Babylon prosper, as if putting him on a level with idols. Two fathers of such gods: the rich man who lavishes gold and the workman who shapes it. They adore what they manufactured. Carry on the shoulder; it cannot answer or save. Remember this: addressed to the Jews as transgressors who, vanquished by a slight temptation, revolted. Return to the heart: forgetfulness of benefits was a sort of madness. Remember the former things: God has testified of himself by numerous proofs at all times. That I am God: he alone; if he admitted any companion, his throne would fall; either there is one God or there is none at all. Declaring from the beginning: taught by constant predictions. My counsel shall stand. Not only foreknowledge: prophecies have no certainty if the same God who declares events did not have the events themselves in his power. Calling a bird or a thought from the east: Cyrus shall come. It may be bird (true signification) or counsel/thought (Dan 2:14); Calvin prefers thought/decree but allows bird as metaphor of sudden approach. Man of my counsel: Cyrus executes the Lord’s decree. From the east / far country: no distance retards God’s work. I have spoken and will accomplish. Hear me, hardened in heart and far from righteousness: Jews almost overwhelmed yet proud; distresses render more rebellious; they refuse the medicine. I bring near my righteousness; it shall not be far off; salvation shall not tarry; I will place salvation in Zion, Israel my glory.

verses.text: Bel bows down; Nebo stoops; their idols are on beasts and livestock; these things you carry are borne as burdens on weary beasts.
verses.arminianNotes:
Bel bows down; Nebo stoops; their idols are on beasts and livestock; these things you carry are borne as burdens on weary beasts. Wesley: Bel—The chief idol of the Babylonians, called by profane historians Jupiter Belus. Boweth—As the Babylonians used to bow down to him to worship, so now he bows down to the victorious Persians. Nebo—Another of the famous idols, which used to deliver oracles. Their idols—Were taken and broken, and the materials of them, gold, silver, and brass, were carried upon beasts into Persia. Your carriages—O ye Persians, to whom he turns his speech.

Arminian hearing: Bel is Jupiter Belus, Nebo the oracle-idol; they bow to the Persians; gold, silver, and brass of the broken images are carried on beasts into Persia; “your carriages” turns the speech to the Persians. Shared loudly with Calvin: historic Bel and Nebo, Babylon’s gods laid low, Persians taking booty; the idols are burdens. Historic Babylon, not a newspaper, not a living politician, not a millennial camp fight. Quote-honesty: Wesley’s “Boweth” is his lemma for ESV “bows down”; “Your carriages” is his lemma for “these things you carry,” not a different verse. Prefer no keyContrast on 1: both camps take historic Bel/Nebo/Persians; Calvin’s farther look to Christ is the larger end, not a millennial fork. Match 45:20: wooden idols that cannot save. Match v. 2: they stoop together and go into captivity.
verses.reformedNotes:

Fulfilled when Persians and Medes took Babylon by storm; idols taken as booty. Isaiah also looked farther to the coming of Christ, when all false worship falls (2 Cor 6:14)—the larger end, not a millennial camp fight. Match v. 2: they cannot save the burden.

Arminian hearing: they are the Babylonians; together means Babylonians and idols, neither helping the other; they could not deliver their idols, and themselves go into captivity. Shared: they stoop together; they cannot save the burden; captivity. Historic Babylon, not a newspaper. Quote-honesty: Wesley’s “Deliver” is his lemma for ESV “they cannot save the burden.” Prefer no keyContrast: both hear idols and worshippers falling together. Match v. 1: Bel and Nebo already bowing. Match v. 3: the God who carries Jacob, unlike these who must be carried.

verses.text: “Listen to me, O house of Jacob, all the remnant of the house of Israel, who have been borne by me from before your birth, carried from the womb;
verses.arminianNotes:

verses.arminianNotes:

Prefer no keyContrast: Wesley has no extra lemma; skip Calvin’s Papist illustration rather than invent a Wesley fight. Match v. 3: the God who carried them. Arminian hearing: though they are unrighteous, he shows himself righteous and faithful, delivering from Babylon after seventy years; the work is saving from the Babylonish captivity; he brings his people to Zion; Israel is the people in whom he will again glory. Shared: I bring near my righteousness; salvation will not delay; salvation in Zion, Israel my glory. Historic Babylon-to-Zion, not a newspaper, not a millennial chart. Quote-honesty: Wesley’s “I bring—Tho’ you are unrighteous” and “Will place—I will bring my people to Zion” are his lemmas for “I bring near my righteousness” and “I will put salvation in Zion”; “Tho’” and “shew” are his spellings. Prefer no keyContrast on 13: both historic Zion after Babylon; skip rather than invent a timetable fight. No open theism: it is not far off; salvation will not delay. Match v. 12: far from righteousness, yet he brings his near. Match 45:13: city built and exiles free.
verses.reformedNotes:
I bring near my righteousness; it is not far off, and my salvation will not delay; I will put salvation in Zion, for Israel my glory. Calvin: I bring near my righteousness; it shall not be far off; salvation shall not tarry; I will place salvation in Zion, Israel my glory. They are far from righteousness; God brings his near. God’s righteousness as fidelity that does not delay; historic Zion after Babylon, not a millennial chart.

Reformed hearing: his righteousness is near, not delayed; salvation placed in Zion; Israel his glory; fidelity does not tarry. Shared with Wesley: I bring near my righteousness; salvation in Zion after Babylon; Israel my glory. Historic Zion after Babylon, not a newspaper, not a millennial chart. Quote-honesty: Calvin’s “I will place salvation in Zion” is his lemma for ESV “I will put salvation in Zion.” Prefer no keyContrast on 13: Wesley’s seventy years / though you are unrighteous overlaps as historic Babylon-to-Zion; skip rather than invent a timetable fight. No open theism: it is not far off; salvation will not delay. Match v. 12: far from righteousness. Match 45:17: everlasting salvation. Match v. 4: I will carry and will save.
